rationale:
The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.fn` only declares the signature `impl Sources { pub async fn search_text(&self, query: &TextQuery) -> Result<TextMatches, SourceError> }`, with the doc comment "Search available project files". The obligations are that the method exists on `Sources`, is async, takes `&TextQuery`, and returns `Result<TextMatches, SourceError>`. Its search semantics belong to the sibling requirements `search_text.behavior` and `search_text.inputs`, so I did not assess them here.

The tests cover those obligations:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It calls `sources.search_text(&TextQuery::new(...))` on a `Sources` value and awaits it. It uses the `Ok` value's `complete` and `matches` (with `.path`), and it asserts that an escaping scope (`SourceScope::under("..")`) returns `Err`. This pins the async method, the `&TextQuery` parameter, the `TextMatches` success type and the fallible `SourceError` result.
- The same test shows the method searches the available project files. A `needle` search finds exactly the 3 non-ignored files. Ignored, `.git` and out-of-root paths are excluded. A scope of `./src/../src` narrows the results to `src/nested.txt`.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[fixed_tools_deliver_domain_contents_with_mandatory_snapshot_dependencies]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]` are also marked. They exercise `search_text` through the agent's fixed tools, which wrap the SDK method. The first asserts the exact match output (`path`, `line`, `excerpt`) for a `disk` pattern. The second runs the search and pages through its results.

I found no gap. Every part of the signature is exercised and its outcome asserted, and the tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.
